AC: Authenticates to the Fidelity 401k via the access path the user ratifies (open decision 1), with 2FA handled and a reusable session so a repeat run does not re-prompt; reads current 401k balance(s) including vested balance where the source exposes it; reads positions / fund allocations as normalized records (fund identifier, description, units, price, value, percent of account); reads contribution history normalized by money source (employee pre-tax, Roth, employer match, catch-up, after-tax) over at least the deepest window the ratified path allows -- 90-day rolling from CSV, or multi-year if quarterly-PDF parsing is ratified (open decision 8); reads fund options per the ratified reading of that term (held funds vs full plan investment lineup, open decision 7); an offline fallback parses hand-downloaded CSV/QIF/PDF so the tool still satisfies the above when the plan disables export or automation is blocked; parsers are unit-tested against redacted fixtures and `make test` is green without network or a browser; no credential or account data is tracked by git; agent-facing documentation states the invocation, the credential/2FA preconditions, the attended-vs-unattended matrix, and the terms-of-service caveat.

Body.raw:
Create a skill or tool for programmatic access to Fidelity 401k retirement
accounts held on the NetBenefits workplace platform: retrieve balances,
positions / fund allocations, contribution history, and fund options, packaged
for agent use. Sibling of the Ameriprise todo 262e8dca (which is itself still
in groom -- there is NO existing Ameriprise tool to model this on, so this
todo is the first financial-account integration in the repo).

## Grooming research findings (2026-08, ratified)

**No participant-facing API exists.** Fidelity's only official APIs are the
WorkplaceXchange B2B catalog (WI Balances API, HRP Participant API, HRP
Election & Loan API, HRP Pay Statements API) at nb.fidelity.com/public/wpx.
These are sold to plan sponsors, payroll vendors and benefits platforms under
contract; an individual plan participant cannot obtain credentials. Treat this
path as closed.

**OFX / Direct Connect is decommissioned.** Fidelity shut off its OFX server
around Dec 2025. Quicken migrated to Express Web Connect Plus (EWC+), a
tokenized Quicken-proprietary channel, and retired "Fidelity NetBenefits" as a
separate financial institution -- 401k data now routes through the "Fidelity
Investments" instance. There is no open OFX endpoint to point a script at.

**Sanctioned aggregation requires being an aggregator.** Fidelity Access,
brokered through Akoya (an FMR spin-out), is the sanctioned no-credential-
sharing channel, and Fidelity actively cut off screen scrapers in Oct 2023.
Plaid listed Fidelity as a supported OAuth institution in Aug 2026 (Link,
/institutions/get, Dashboard). Open question below: whether Plaid's Fidelity
coverage includes workplace NetBenefits plan accounts at all, and whether
Plaid /investments/holdings and /investments/transactions carry 401k-specific
fields (contribution money-source, vesting, plan fund lineup) -- they likely do
not. Plaid also needs a developer account and paid production access.

**Browser automation is the only path an individual controls.** Working prior
art, all Playwright-based: eebette/bank_scrapers (module
bank_scrapers.scrapers.fidelity_netbenefits.driver.get_accounts_info -- logs
in, handles MFA via an OTP-code file, and downloads the positions export
rather than scraping the DOM), kennyboy106/fidelity-api (positions, balances,
order placement; playwright + pyotp; GPL -- a licensing decision for this
REUSE-managed repo), KuphJr/fidelipy (semi-automated trading only, manual
login), and TylerFlar/claude-fidelity-mcp (MCP server exposing
fidelity_get_accounts / fidelity_get_positions, TOTP or SMS 2FA, persisted
session state under ~/.fidelity-mcp, Playwright Firefox). Automating the web
interface may violate Fidelity's customer agreement, and the login is fronted
by commercial bot detection where headless is materially more detectable than
headed.

**Data ceilings that shape the AC.** The one-click Positions CSV on
fidelity.com covers 401k accounts when the plan permits. Activity /
transaction CSV downloads are capped at a 90-day window per download and the
column schema differs by account type, so any multi-year contribution history
needs windowed downloads plus dedup/merge. Some employer plans disable CSV
export entirely. NetBenefits itself offers a QIF transaction download under
"Accounts & Benefits / View your Transaction history / Download Transaction
History" but no downloadable positions file. The per-source contribution
breakdown the AC needs (employee pre-tax, Roth, employer match, catch-up,
after-tax) reliably appears only in the quarterly PDF statements, which
Fidelity retains for ~10 years.

**Repo has no precedent.** No browser automation, no credential loader, no
financial tooling exists here. The nearest convention is thermo/PRIV.md:
gitignored priv/ directories holding plaintext secret files, with public
counterparts under config/. Playwright and a project .venv are new
infrastructure for this repo.

## OPEN DECISIONS -- blocked on user, do not guess

1. **Access path.** Browser automation with your own credentials, a
   Plaid/Akoya aggregator integration, or offline-only (the tool never logs
   in; you download files by hand and it parses a drop directory)? This gates
   every item below.
2. **Your plan's login topology.** Does netbenefits.com accept a standalone
   Fidelity username/password for your plan, or is it reachable only via
   employer SSO from a benefits portal? Does your 401k appear in the
   fidelity.com Positions view (unified login) or only on NetBenefits?
3. **MFA shape.** Is an authenticator-app TOTP secret enrolled and
   extractable (unattended runs possible via pyotp), or is the account
   SMS/push-only (attended runs only, with an OTP handoff)?
4. **Write operations.** The AC is read-only. Are contribution-rate changes,
   fund exchanges / rebalancing, and loan operations in scope, explicitly out
   of scope, or deferred? Recommendation: explicitly out of scope -- ERISA
   plan mutations have a large blast radius and no dry-run.
5. **Credential storage.** Gitignored priv/ file per thermo/PRIV.md, OS
   keyring, pass/GPG, environment variables, or no storage at all (prompt per
   run)? Related: where does the retrieved financial data land, and is that
   path gitignored?
6. **Terms-of-service risk.** Automating the Fidelity web interface likely
   violates the customer agreement and risks account lockout on a retirement
   account. Do you accept that risk, and with what rate-limit discipline?
7. **What "fund options" means in the AC.** The funds you currently hold
   (present in the positions export) or the plan's full available investment
   lineup (NetBenefits-only page, no export, DOM scraping)? Materially
   different work.
8. **Contribution history depth.** Is quarterly-statement PDF parsing in
   scope to get money-source detail and history beyond the 90-day CSV window,
   or is a 90-day rolling window acceptable?
9. **Packaging and location.** New utils/fidelity/ project with its own
   .venv, or a shared utils/finance/ module? Standalone CLI, MCP server, or a
   markdown skill under skills/ wrapping a CLI? Scope.path_from_root is
   deliberately left unset until this is answered.
10. **Relationship to Ameriprise 262e8dca.** Design a shared
    auth/session/normalization abstraction up front, or land Fidelity
    standalone and let Ameriprise refactor toward it afterwards?

## Child plan

Recommended shape is parent-local WorkItems only: one project directory, one
subsystem, one branch artifact. If the user authorizes fan-out, the two
independent fact-finding domains that would justify subtodos are the
sanctioned-path evaluation (Plaid/Akoya feasibility) and the prior-art
evaluation (bank_scrapers / fidelity-api / claude-fidelity-mcp against the
real account); those are unrelated toolchains and could run in parallel, each
landing a notes commit, with the parent staying synthesis-only. Everything
after the decision gate is sequential.

## USER DECISION (2026-08-23): playwright-mcp as human proxy

Access approach decided: use playwright-mcp to interact with NetBenefits/Fidelity as a normal human proxy, NOT as automated scraping. The agent drives the browser on behalf of the user, with the user able to intervene for 2FA, SSO, or unusual flows. This:
- Resolves Decision #1 (access path): browser automation via playwright-mcp
- Reframes Decision #6 (ToS risk): human-proxied interaction, not bot scraping
- Changes the auth model: human remains in the loop for MFA, reducing lockout risk
- Aligns with Ameriprise approach (262e8dca) for consistency

LongSummary.raw:
Programmatic read access to a Fidelity 401k held on the NetBenefits workplace
platform, packaged as an agent-usable skill or CLI: account balances,
positions and fund allocations, contribution history broken down by money
source, and the plan's fund options. It is the repo's first financial-account
integration; the sibling Ameriprise todo 262e8dca is also still ungroomed, so
there is no in-repo precedent for credential handling, browser automation, or
normalized account records to copy from.

Grooming research settled the feasible access paths. Fidelity publishes no
participant-facing API -- the WorkplaceXchange catalog (WI Balances API, HRP
Participant API, HRP Election & Loan API) is contracted to plan sponsors and
payroll vendors, not individuals. Fidelity decommissioned its OFX server
around December 2025, and Quicken's replacement Express Web Connect Plus is a
proprietary tokenized channel with NetBenefits retired as a separate
institution. Fidelity Access, brokered through Akoya, is the sanctioned
credential-free channel but requires being a contracted aggregator; Plaid
listed Fidelity as an OAuth institution in August 2026, though whether its
coverage reaches workplace NetBenefits plan accounts, and whether
/investments/holdings carries 401k money-source and fund-lineup detail,
remains unverified. That leaves Playwright browser automation as the only path
an individual controls, with usable prior art in eebette/bank_scrapers
(fidelity_netbenefits driver, MFA handling, downloads the positions export),
kennyboy106/fidelity-api (GPL, a licensing question for this REUSE-managed
repo), and TylerFlar/claude-fidelity-mcp (TOTP plus persisted session state).
Automating the web interface likely violates Fidelity's customer agreement,
and the login sits behind commercial bot detection that treats headless
browsers as more suspicious than headed ones.

Data availability, not scraping mechanics, is the binding constraint. The
one-click Positions CSV covers 401k accounts when the plan permits it;
activity and transaction CSV downloads are capped at a rolling 90-day window
with account-type-dependent columns, so multi-year history needs windowed
downloads plus dedup and merge. Some employer plans disable CSV export
outright. NetBenefits offers a QIF transaction download but no positions file,
and the per-source contribution breakdown the acceptance criteria call for
(employee pre-tax, Roth, employer match, catch-up, after-tax) appears
reliably only in quarterly PDF statements. An offline fallback that parses
hand-downloaded CSV, QIF and PDF from a drop directory is therefore planned as
a real path, not a consolation prize.

Ten decisions are deliberately left to the user rather than guessed, and the
work items are gated behind them: which access path to take, whether the
plan's NetBenefits login is standalone or employer-SSO-only, whether an
extractable TOTP secret exists (unattended runs) or the account is SMS-only
(attended runs), whether write operations such as contribution-rate changes,
fund exchanges and loans are in scope (recommended out of scope), how
credentials and harvested financial data are stored relative to the
gitignored priv/ convention in thermo/PRIV.md, whether the terms-of-service
and account-lockout risk is accepted, whether "fund options" means held funds
or the plan's full investment lineup, whether quarterly PDF parsing is in
scope, where the project lives and in what form (Scope.path_from_root is
deliberately unset pending this), and whether a shared abstraction with the
Ameriprise work is designed up front or refactored toward later.

WorkItems.summary: [HICAP] Decision gate -- do not write code before this closes. Walk the user through the 10 OPEN DECISIONS in Body (access path; plan login topology; MFA shape; write ops in/out of scope; credential + data storage; ToS risk acceptance; meaning of 'fund options'; contribution-history depth; packaging/location incl. Scope.path_from_root; Ameriprise 262e8dca sharing). Record the ratified answers in Body, rewrite LongSummary in the same breath, and re-groom the items below to match.

[MIDCAP] Spike A -- observed topology of the real plan (attended, no credentials committed). Log in by hand to netbenefits.com and fidelity.com and record: whether one Fidelity username/password reaches both; whether the 401k appears in the fidelity.com Positions view; whether the Positions CSV download is offered for it; whether NetBenefits 'Accounts & Benefits / View your Transaction history / Download Transaction History' offers CSV and/or QIF and over what date window; whether a plan investment-options page exists. Land findings as a notes file with account numbers redacted.

[MIDCAP] Spike B -- sanctioned paths, go/no-go. Determine whether Plaid's Fidelity OAuth institution exposes workplace NetBenefits plan accounts at all, and whether /investments/holdings and /investments/transactions carry 401k money-source, vesting and plan fund-lineup fields; capture Plaid production-access requirements and cost; confirm Fidelity Access/Akoya is contract-only for individuals. Written recommendation, no integration code.

[MIDCAP] Prior-art evaluation against the real account, headed mode. Try eebette/bank_scrapers (bank_scrapers.scrapers.fidelity_netbenefits.driver), kennyboy106/fidelity-api, and TylerFlar/claude-fidelity-mcp; record which actually reaches 401k data (not just retail brokerage), how each handles MFA and session persistence, maintenance state, and license -- fidelity-api is GPL, which is a REUSE.toml/licensing decision for this repo. Conclude: vendor, depend, or reimplement.

[MIDCAP] Scaffold the project per AGENTS.md. Create the chosen project dir, run ./create_pipenv.sh on it, commit only .venv/README.md as the marker, write requirements.txt (playwright + ratified deps), a Makefile whose 'test' target is fast (fixtures only, no network, no browser) and whose 'all-tests' target owns the browser/e2e suite, .www/blurb.md, and REUSE headers. Set Scope.path_from_root to match.

[HICAP] Login exemplar -- one bounded implementation, then roll out on MIDCAP. Playwright login to the ratified host, headed-first with an explicit headless opt-in, persisted storage_state for session reuse plus expiry detection and re-login, TOTP via pyotp when a secret is enrolled and an interactive OTP handoff when it is not, and conservative pacing so repeated runs do not trip bot detection or lock the retirement account. Guard tests exercise the state machine against recorded fixtures, never the live site.

[MIDCAP] Credential and secret handling per the ratified storage decision. Loader that keeps secrets out of the repo, out of argv and out of process listings; gitignore entries for both the credential path and the retrieved-data output path; redaction in logs, error messages and any Playwright screenshots/traces. Unit test asserts a secret value never reaches stdout, stderr or an artifact file.

[MIDCAP] Balances and positions retrieval. Drive the positions export for the 401k (download the file rather than scraping the DOM where the site offers it) and normalize to a stable record schema: account id, plan name, fund identifier (ticker and/or CUSIP), description, units, price, value, percent of account, and vested balance where exposed. Emit JSON and CSV. Parser unit-tested against a redacted fixture; no live-site dependency in the fast suite.

[MIDCAP] Contribution history retrieval. Drive the NetBenefits transaction-history download (CSV and/or QIF per Spike A) with automatic windowing around the 90-day per-download cap, then dedup and merge across windows into one ordered series; normalize each row's money source (employee pre-tax, Roth, employer match, catch-up, after-tax) and transaction type. Fixture-based parser tests covering both the CSV and QIF shapes and the window-boundary overlap.

[MIDCAP] Fund options retrieval, per the ratified reading of open decision 7. Either restrict to held funds already present in the positions export, or scrape the plan's investment-options page for the full available lineup; normalize ticker/CUSIP, fund name, category and expense ratio where available. If the full lineup is chosen, note that this is DOM scraping with no export behind it and is therefore the most brittle surface in the tool.

[MIDCAP] Offline-input fallback -- required, not optional, because some employer plans disable CSV export entirely and automation may be blocked. Parse hand-downloaded artifacts from a drop directory: positions CSV, transaction CSV/QIF, and (if open decision 8 ratifies it) quarterly statement PDFs for the money-source contribution breakdown Fidelity retains ~10 years. Same normalized output schema as the automated path, exercised by the same fixture tests.

[MIDCAP] CLI surface over the retrievals: balances | positions | contributions | funds subcommands with --json/--csv, --out, --since/--until, --offline <dir> and --dry-run; consistent exit codes; a clear error when the session is expired or MFA input is required. Wire it to the package entry point and add a smoke test that runs every subcommand against fixtures.

[MIDCAP] Agent-facing documentation. Write the skill doc plus README covering when to invoke the tool, the subcommands and their output schema, credential and 2FA preconditions, the attended-vs-unattended matrix (TOTP secret present vs SMS-only), rate-limit and account-lockout cautions, the terms-of-service caveat, and the offline fallback procedure. Add .www/blurb.md and run 'make index' at the repo root.

[LOCAP] Run and report: recreate the project .venv from scratch, confirm (cd <project>; make test) is green with no network and no browser, run the REUSE lint, and audit 'git ls-files' plus the working tree for any credential, account number or downloaded statement that must not be tracked. Report results verbatim; escalate any red to MIDCAP for the fix, not for a re-run.

[LOCAP] Feed the outcome back to the Ameriprise todo 262e8dca: append the reusable pieces (session/storage_state handling, credential loader, normalized position and transaction schema, offline-drop-directory fallback) to its Body via todo.py set so it inherits these decisions instead of rediscovering them.
